scenario: Marine-tourism researchers study only reef-tour operators that survived three or more consecutive storm seasons; their mean annual revenue is $4.2M (σ=$0.9M). The survival threshold is $2.5M annual revenue. Researchers want the true mean revenue across all operators before attrition.

data.description: Observed statistics among units that cleared the survival/publication filter

question: (a) Assuming annual revenue is normally distributed with σ=0.9 million USD, solve for the pre-filter true mean μ such that E[X|X>2.5]=4.2. (b) What fraction of all original units cleared the survival filter? (c) By how much does the observed (survivor) mean overstate the pre-filter true mean?

ground_truth.explanation: The reef-tour operators surviving repeated storm seasons annual revenue set is a truncated-normal sample above the 2.5 threshold. Solving E[X|X>2.5]=μ+σφ((2.5−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((2.5−μ)/σ)=4.2 gives μ≈4.12744. Only 96.5% of all original units survived; the survivor mean overstates the true mean by 0.0726 million USD.

naive_answer: The true mean annual revenue is 4.2 million USD because that is the observed average among reef-tour operators surviving repeated storm seasons.
naive_trap: Survival/publication filters truncate the distribution from below; the observed mean among survivors is a conditional expectation and systematically overstates the pre-filter population mean.
reasoning_trace: (1) Survival filter is equivalent to truncated-normal sampling above threshold=2.5. (2) Truncated mean equation: μ+σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=4.2. (3) Numerically solve with brentq → μ≈4.12744. (4) Fraction surviving: Φ̄((2.5−4.12744)/σ)≈0.96472.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 4.2,0.9,2.5
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-20*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=200)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-4.12744)<0.005
assert abs(frac-0.96472)<0.005
assert mu_sol < obs
